warnings.title: Yellow thunderstorm warning
warnings.description:
Information on update: A band of heavy rain in the west will move slowly eastwards over the next few hours, before showers develop more widely later this morning. Warning start time brought forward. Heavy showers will develop Tuesday morning, becoming heavy and locally thundery into the afternoon. Whilst some areas will miss these, where they do develop they will be slow-moving, bringing 20-30 mm of rain in an hour or two. Strong and gusty winds and hail will also be possible with the heaviest showers.

Showers should slowly ease from the west into the evening.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings
warnings.instruction:
Consider if your location is at risk of flash flooding. If so, consider preparing a flood plan and an 
emergency flood kit.  

Give yourself the best chance of avoiding delays by checking road conditions if driving, or bus and 
train timetables, amending your travel plans if necessary. 

People cope better with power cuts when they have prepared for them in advance. It’s easy to do; 
consider gathering torches and batteries, a mobile phone power pack and other essential items.
 
If you find yourself outside and hear thunder, protect yourself by finding a safe enclosed shelter 
(such as a car). Do not shelter under or near trees, or other structures which may be struck by 
lightning. If you are on an elevated area move to lower ground. 

Be prepared for weather warnings to change quickly: when a weather warning is issued, the Met 
Office recommends staying up to date with the weather forecast in your area.

Whilst not all places in the warning area will see heavy showers, accumulations of 15 to 20 mm are possible in 1 hour and 30 to 40 mm in 3 hours or so where they do occur. Hail and lightning will be additional hazards.

warnings.title: Yellow thunderstorm warning
warnings.description:
Heavy, slow-moving showers and some thunderstorms are likely to break out from late morning. Along with lightning, gusty winds and some hail, these will have the potential to give 20-30mm of rain in 1-2 hours and perhaps 50mm in a few places over 3-6 hours. This may lead to localised flash flooding, and impacts to the transport network.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings
warnings.instruction:
Consider if your location is at risk of flash flooding. If so, consider preparing a flood plan and an emergency flood kit.
 
Prepare to protect your property and people from injury. Before gusty winds arrive, check to ensure moveable objects or temporary structures are well secured. Items include; bins, garden furniture, trampolines, tents, gazebos, sheds, and fences.

Give yourself the best chance of avoiding delays by checking road conditions if driving, or bus and train timetables, amending your travel plans if necessary.

People cope better with power cuts when they have prepared for them in advance. It’s easy to do; consider gathering torches and batteries, a mobile phone power pack and other essential items.

If you find yourself outside and hear thunder, protect yourself by finding a safe enclosed shelter (such as a car). Do not shelter under or near trees, or other structures which may be struck by lightning. If you are on an elevated area move to lower ground.

Be prepared for weather warnings to change quickly: when a weather warning is issued, the Met Office recommends staying up to date with the weather forecast in your area.
